messages:
rachel: FYI I hit a weird one on Ubuntu 22.04 with the tarball install + systemd unit. localserve started at boot using the wrong profile (prod) and immediately prompted for interactive login even though we set --profile staging in the unit file.
omar: Hmm. can you paste the ExecStart line from the unit and the unit file contents?
rachel: ExecStart=/opt/redwood/redwoodctl localserve --profile staging --config /etc/redwood/config.yaml
rachel: But journal shows: reading profile /home/redwood/.config/redwood/profiles/default.json and then `interactive login required` and systemd restarts it repeatedly.
sudha: Is the unit running as the redwood user? If systemd uses a different HOME or EnvironmentFile it could be resolving config from /root or the system account.
omar: Also check if the unit is a simple Service vs a Type=forking wrapper that reexecs. Sometimes wrappers drop args.
cli-bot: Quick diagnostic suggestion: run `systemctl cat redwood-local.service` and `ps -o cmd --pid $(systemctl show -p MainPID --value redwood-local)` after start. Also try `strace -f -e execve -s200 -p <pid>` to see actual argv passed.
rachel: systemctl cat:
```
[Unit]
Description=Redwood LocalServe
After=network.target

[Service]
User=redwood
WorkingDirectory=/home/redwood
ExecStart=/opt/redwood/redwoodctl localserve --profile staging --config /etc/redwood/config.yaml
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```
rachel: ps shows child process invoked as `/opt/redwood/redwoodctl localserve` (no --profile or --config).
omar: That confirms the binary is being exec'd without args. Maybe the unit launches a wrapper script in the tarball that spawns the real binary and doesn't forward args, or the execve call is shadowed by an install-time symlink.
sudha: Any env vars set? `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE` or `REDWOOD_CONFIG` could be clobbered by a system-wide env file. Check /etc/default/redwood or /etc/systemd/system/redwood-local.service.d/*.conf.
rachel: No overrides. Also tried setting Environment=REDWOODCTL_PROFILE=staging in the unit, same result: journald shows env but child still uses default profile. Logs: 
```
[2024-06-18T07:10:01Z] args: ["/opt/redwood/redwoodctl", "localserve"]
[2024-06-18T07:10:01Z] env: REDWOODCTL_PROFILE=staging
[2024-06-18T07:10:01Z] resolving config: /home/redwood/.config/redwood/profiles/default.json
[2024-06-18T07:10:01Z] auth: interactive login required
```
omar: That is weird. If args/env are present the binary should pick profile. Could this be an early init where it reads a config copy baked into the tarball under /opt/redwood/default-profiles? Maybe packaging step wrote a default and the binary prefers that path when launched by systemd (no tty).
sudha: Another angle: when launched without a TTY the binary might treat stdin closed and enter a non-interactive auth flow that forces token refresh and then falls back to default profile. But that doesn't explain missing args.
cli-bot: Suggestion: check for setuid bit or a setuid helper binary that drops arguments. Also inspect any wrapper at /opt/redwood/redwoodctl (is it a shell script or a symlink?). `file /opt/redwood/redwoodctl && head -n 20 /opt/redwood/redwoodctl`
rachel: It's a small shell stub: `#!/bin/sh\nexec /opt/redwood/bin/redwoodctl.real "$@"` — so it should forward args. But journal shows only `localserve` being passed to the real binary, not the flags. Could systemd be passing args differently because ExecStart uses a shell? We used ExecStart with a full command line not an array.
omar: systemd passes the whole ExecStart string to the shell only if you prefix with /bin/sh -c. Since you used the binary path it should exec directly. But the presence of a shell script stub means /opt/redwood/redwoodctl is the script and `exec /opt/redwood/bin/redwoodctl.real "$@"` should forward. Strange.
sudha: Maybe there's a quoting/parsing bug in the stub: if `redwoodctl` is installed with CRLF line endings or weird quoting it could chop args. Also check for `argv0` replacement in the real binary where it inspects os.Args[0] and accidentally parses embedded args from argv0 like `redwoodctl localserve` — some packagers do that.
rachel: I ran `strace -f -e execve` on the mainpid and saw: `execve("/opt/redwood/bin/redwoodctl.real", ["/opt/redwood/bin/redwoodctl.real", "localserve"], [/* 20 vars */]) = 0`. So indeed args missing. The stub passed only the subcommand. The unit's ExecStart had the full flags though.
omar: Could be systemd escaping: if ExecStart uses an absolute path to a script that isn't marked as ExecStart arguments get split weirdly. Try using ExecStart=/bin/sh -c '/opt/redwood/redwoodctl localserve --profile staging --config /etc/redwood/config.yaml' to force full parsing, or prefer ExecStartPre that writes a unit-specific env file.
sudha: I'll open RDW-DEVEX-1401: systemd/Tarball packaging: args lost when stubbed binary is a shell wrapper. Labels: linux, packaging, cli. Link: https://redwood.internal/issue/RDW-DEVEX-1401
devex-bot: New issue RDW-DEVEX-1401 created by sudha. Priority: P2.
rachel: Temporary workaround that fixed it: replace ExecStart with the real binary path `/opt/redwood/bin/redwoodctl.real localserve --profile staging --config /etc/redwood/config.yaml` and it now reads staging and login is non-interactive (token present).
omar: Good. We'll update tarball packaging to either make the stub a proper execable binary that forwards args safely or include a systemd unit template that uses the real binary. Also add a note in Install docs for tarball users about systemd ExecStart pitfalls.
sudha: I'll assign packaging and eng-cli to coordinate. Also adding a regression test that bundles systemd unit and validates args are forwarded on install.
rachel: Thanks all. Leaving unit and strace logs in the ticket for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
